title: Semantic I/O Contract Matrix and Regression Harness for Pinned Model Releases
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and implement a machine-readable Semantic I/O Contract Matrix for pinned model versions that captures required prompt formats, canonical output shapes, stable parameter enums, and published performance profiles (latency/cost/quality). Build an automated regression harness and CI gate that validates new model binaries against the matrix before a pinned-version promotion. The goal is to prevent silent behavior shifts for customers who pin versions and to publish a deterministic 'stability fingerprint' used by Console and the model catalog.
acceptance_criteria: A contract matrix schema (YAML/JSON) is finalized and checked into model-catalog/specs with fields for input templates, required system messages, allowed parameter ranges, deterministic-output expectations, and perf-profile references.
Every pinned model in onboarding has an accompanying manifest that implements the schema and is discoverable via the API and Console.

A regression harness (unit + integration) runs in CI that: (a) replays canonical prompt suite, (b) measures token-level diffs, embedding drift, and latency/cost regressions, and (c) fails gating PRs if thresholds are exceeded.
Console shows a published 'stability fingerprint' (hash + human-readable summary) and links to the perf profile for each pinned version.
Rollout playbook documented: steps for devs to update contracts, deprecation policy for breaking changes, and communication checklist for affected customers.
Perf profiles are published in the model catalog as versioned artifacts (latency percentiles, cost/unit estimates, and token-efficiency tips).

decisions: Use a single extensible JSON/YAML schema (semio-contract-v1) rather than multiple ad-hoc files to simplify validation and Console rendering.
Stability fingerprint will be computed as a combination of a stable schema-hash + a hash of the canonical output set (deterministic subset) and published as semio:v1:hex.
Regression harness will be part of the model onboarding pipeline and also runnable locally by model maintainers using the dockerized runner.
Perf profiles will be stored as separate versioned artifacts and referenced from the contract manifest; this lets us update perf numbers independently of I/O contracts.

Deviations that are intentionally non-breaking (e.g., improved latency with identical outputs) will be allowed but must include a justification field in the manifest and a test that demonstrates semantic equivalence.
Breaks to required system messages or output schema are considered breaking changes and require a new pinned version; automated CI must fail promotion in such cases.
test_plan: Unit tests for contract schema validation (negative + positive cases).
Integration tests that: (1) pull candidate model artifact, (2) run canonical prompt suite, (3) compute token diffs and embedding drift, (4) run latency/cost profiler, (5) assert thresholds.
Nightly job that re-runs regression harness against a small sample of pinned versions to detect bitrot or hardware-induced drift.
Chaos test: simulate quantization fallback to ensure fallback models referenced in manifest preserve declared output_shape and parameter enums.
Manual review checklist for borderline CI failures (provide diff viewer, example inputs/outputs, and suggested rollback PR template).
